To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the best floral stages to excise anthers for eggplant anther culture are younger than those previously described in the literature, and that the morphological characteristics used to identify them may be different for each accession.
the stage of anther culture and heterostylic status of the cultivar have a significant effect on the induction of eggplant embryogenesis.

(a) the best anther stage to culture for embryogenesis induction is the youngest one, with a high proportion of young and mid microsopres, (b) the anther wall thickness may be a limiting factor in the efficiency of the culture and (c) heterostyly does not affect the efficiency of anthers for embryogenesis induction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two aspects of egg plant flower biology, potentially involved on the success of anther culture.
the improvement of the embryogenesis induction from anther cultures in eggplant, and may contribute with the development of new breeding strategies in this species.
the optimization of anther culture protocols in eggplant, and with the identification of the best floral stages and buds for anther excisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the most responsive anther culture stage is the one in which the majority of anthers are in a stage of young to mid microspores, and that the most responsive buds are those in a stage of mid microspores and bicellular pollen.

the most efficient floral stage for embryogenesis induction is the one in which the majority of anthers contain young microspores, and that this stage is reached earlier in the development of anthers with thin walls than in those with thick walls.

the stage of anther extraction for eggplant anther culture is not as important as the stage of microspores and pollen present in the anther, and that the latter is the most important factor to be considered for successful embryogenesis induction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for eggplant anther culture, the best floral buds and anthers to excise are those containing the most vacuolated microspores, and that the most responsive anthers are the youngest, containing mostly mid microspores, regardless of the floral morph.

anther culture in eggplant may be optimized by: (i) selecting buds and anthers containing microspores at the mid to young stages, and (ii) using buds of the same morph, since the embryogenic response is similar.
, in eggplant, the stage of microspores for anther culture should be younger than previously thought, and the floral morph of the plant is not relevant for the efficiency of the culture.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the selection of the most responsive anthers for culture may not be the best choice.
the stage of the floral bud to be used for anther culture is not the same for all eggplant cultivars.
the selection of the floral stage and the morphs for eggplant anther culture may not be the most critical aspects for embryogenesis induction.
